verdict.rationale: Warp's Automation Platform documents event triggers: cloud agents can react to events from Slack, Linear, GitHub, or custom webhooks, and can be triggered by system events. That is first-party support for event-driven automatic actions. However, the evidence only names the trigger feature. It does not show how users define the rules themselves, such as conditions, filters, matching logic, or mapping events to specific actions. Schedules are time-based recurring runs, not event triggers, so they are not credited here. Missing for 10: documented rule-definition syntax with conditions/filters, detail on configuring which action runs for which event, and independent or hands-on corroboration that triggers work as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Triggers: React to events from Slack, Linear, GitHub, or custom webhooks
Cloud agents are autonomous, background agents that run on Warp’s cloud infrastructure or your own, triggered by system events, schedules, or integrations like Slack and GitHub.
The Automation Platform runs cloud agents from triggers, schedules, integrations, and APIs.
